title: Recording Well and Craniotomy for Electrophysiology in Head-Restrained Mice
author: Susu Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9a8h2hw

steps.title: Prepare and Anesthetize Animal
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for surgery using anesthesia and stabilization.

substeps.instruction: Disinfect all surgery tools and the headbar.
Anesthetize the animal with 3% Isoflurane.
Mount the animal onto a stereotaxic frame with a homeothermic heating pad underneath.
Adjust isoflurane to 1~1.5% to maintain a steady breathing rate of ~1/sec and keep body temperature at 37 °C.
Verify absence of reflexes by pinching the toe.

steps.title: Administer Pre-operative Medications
steps.instruction: Provide local anesthesia, pain relief, and eye protection.

substeps.instruction: Inject 0.1 ml of 0.5% marcaine (local anaesthetic) under the scalp for topical anesthesia.
Administer 5 mg/kg Ketoprofen (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug) subcutaneously.
Apply eye gel or ointment to the eyes to prevent drying.

steps.title: Prepare Skull and Level Head
steps.instruction: Clean the surgical site and align the skull for precise implantation.

substeps.instruction: Clean the scalp and hair with 70% ethanol and betadine.
Remove the scalp with a single cut from between the ears to between the eyes.
Remove protruding hairs using scissors and cotton swabs.
Clean the skull thoroughly with saline, followed by 70% ethanol, and dry with sterile cotton swabs.
Mark key reference points (e.g., Bregma, Lambda, and craniotomy locations) using a fine-tip permanent marker.
Level Bregma and Lambda to within 40 μm of each other along the dorsal-ventral axis.
Level two additional points (± 2 mm lateral to Bregma) to within 40 μm of each other along the dorsal-ventral axis.

steps.title: Implant Titanium Headbar
steps.instruction: Secure the headbar to the skull using adhesive.

substeps.instruction: Roughen the skull surface at the headbar implantation site using a slowly turning dental drill.
Apply an even layer of Krazy glue to the skull surface and position the titanium headbar.
Cover the headbar with a thick layer of Krazy glue and allow it to dry.

steps.title: Construct Recording Well
steps.instruction: Build a reinforced recording well using dental acrylic/cement.

substeps.instruction: Apply dental acrylic/cement over the glue layer using a 50 µl pipette tip (use a thin mixture to avoid bubbles).
Gradually add layers of dental cement around the skull edge to build a convex-shaped recording well.
Allow dental acrylic to cure between adding layers.
Ensure the recording well is at least 4 mm in height and capable of holding at least 0.1 ml of cortex buffer.

steps.title: Post-Implantation Recovery
steps.instruction: Provide post-operative analgesia and recovery monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Remove the animal from the stereotaxic frame.
Inject 0.05 mg/kg Buprenorphine (Opioid analgesic) into the intraperitoneal (IP) cavity.
Place the animal in a temperature-controlled cage (37 °C) until it is ambulatory.

steps.title: Perform Craniotomy
steps.instruction: Create openings in the skull on the day before the first acute recording.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal following the procedure in Step 1.
Label the center/edge of each craniotomy based on previously marked reference points.
Drill one craniotomy at a time (approximately 1-1.5 mm diameter) to create an 'island', typically requiring 10-20 rounds of drilling.
Clear bone debris with compressed air and rinse the skull with cortex buffer between rounds to prevent tissue heating and swelling.
Stop drilling when a thin layer of bone remains; apply cortex buffer on top.
Gently push the center to ensure the bone edge is thin enough to break.
Lift the bone flap with fine forceps while the surface is covered in cortex buffer.
Apply cortex buffer-soaked Gelfoam to the dura surface to control small bleeders.

steps.title: Perform Durotomy (If Required)
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the dura from the craniotomy site.

substeps.instruction: Select a clean spot without surface blood vessels on the corner or edge of the craniotomy.
Make a small incision into the dura using a fresh 31 gauge needle at a shallow angle.
Insert the lower jaw of fine-tip forceps into the incision almost parallel to the brain surface.
Tightly grab and pull the dura across the craniotomy, avoiding contact with the underlying cortex.
Remove any remaining attached flaps of dura using the same grab-and-pull method, avoiding large surface blood vessels.
Use Gelfoam soaked in cortex buffer to manage small bleeders.
Perform all steps in cortex buffer and rinse the site with additional cortex buffer to remove debris.
Drill all craniotomies sequentially until bone flaps are ready to be lifted one-by-one in cortex buffer.
If drilling new craniotomies on a skull with existing open ones, cover previous craniotomies with Kwik-cast to prevent debris contamination.

steps.title: Seal Recording Well
steps.instruction: Seal the surgical site and recover the animal.

substeps.instruction: Absorb all cortex buffer with a sugi sponge, ensuring the dura/brain surface remains moist but without excessive liquid.
Apply Kwik-cast sealant to cover the craniotomies/durotomies.
Remove the animal from the stereotaxic frame and place it in a temperature-controlled cage (37 °C) until ambulatory.
